The problem

Growing a business takes more than scattered tools.

Every merchant we talk to is stuck on the same three things.

Agencies charge monthly whether it works or not

You pay the retainer, get the report, and still run the follow-ups yourself. Results are optional; the invoice is not.

Ad accounts need attention every single day

Budgets drift, creatives fatigue, audiences saturate. Miss a day and money burns on a campaign that already broke.

Content for every channel is a full-time job

Captions, ads, WhatsApp messages, organic posts — each channel wants different content, constantly. Nobody has that bandwidth.

The product

Every problem between a merchant and growth, solved in one place.

Six things the platform does that otherwise need an agency, an ops hire and a spreadsheet.

Ads that manage themselves

Campaigns launched, optimised and rotated from the catalogue. Budgets pace, creatives refresh before they fatigue, ROAS tracked live — no daily babysitting.

Carts recovered on WhatsApp

A message within minutes of every abandoned checkout, with who came back and what each message earned. Recovery becomes a revenue line, not a lucky guess.

Attribution that settles arguments

Meta CAPI, GA4 and store orders combined into one view. Every pound is tied to a real outcome instead of a gut feeling.

Content generated and scheduled

Product captions, ad copy, WhatsApp broadcasts and organic posts in Arabic and English, published on a schedule nobody has to keep.

Customers who come back

After every order a sequence starts — thank you, review request, upsell, re-engagement. The customers already won keep buying, with no manual follow-up.

One place to see everything

Team, agency or VA invited with permissions. Every ad, message, post and analytics action logged and visible, so nobody wonders what is running.

How it works

Set it up once. The business grows itself.

Three steps, then a schedule the merchant controls.

  1. 01

    Ads launch, carts are recovered, content goes out, customers are brought back and revenue is tracked, on a schedule the merchant sets.

The mechanism

Two ways in to every integration.

This is the part that is genuinely unusual, and it is the reason the platform ages well.

REST for automation

Webhooks and background sync — the conventional path every integration supports.

MCP for AI-native access

The same connections exposed for real-time conversational control. An AI agent can read and act on the merchant's store, ads and inbox directly rather than through a scraper.

One internal model

Orders, catalogue and customers are the platform's own shapes. Connectors map into them, which is why adding the next storefront is scheduled work rather than a rewrite.

Standalone or connected

A merchant can run everything on OurGrowth alone, or keep the store they already sell through. Neither path is a migration and neither is a lock-in.

The model

Flat rate. No surprises.

Priced so a merchant can predict it, and so the incentive is retention rather than billable hours.

Monthly subscription

A flat fee per merchant. No share of ad spend, no share of revenue, no line item that grows when they succeed. A 14-day trial with no card.

Multi-tenant

Every merchant is an isolated tenant on shared infrastructure — the reason the marginal cost of the next customer is small.

Two markets, one engine

Egypt and the Gulf differ in courier, currency and payment rail, not in product. The same platform serves both.

Managed tier

For merchants who want it done rather than run: the same platform with an operator behind it, at a higher monthly rate.

Roadmap

Where the next value is.

Each of these is an integration or a market, not a research project — which is what makes the sequence schedulable.

  1. P1

    The COD platforms

    EasyOrders is Egypt's leading OMS for cash on delivery. It is the connector that matches the platform's core buyer most exactly.

  2. P2

    The Saudi storefronts

    Salla and Zid are the Arabic-first platforms merchants in the Kingdom actually use. They open the second market properly.

  3. P3

    The long tail

    WooCommerce and YouCan across North Africa. Same internal model, more surface area.

  4. P4

    Managed at scale

    The same platform with an operator behind it, sold to merchants who want the outcome rather than the tool.

The ask

What the money is for.

The build is behind us. What is missing is distribution.

  • Merchant acquisitionA repeatable way to reach cash-on-delivery merchants in Egypt and the Gulf, measured on cost per paying merchant.
  • Finish the connectorsFive storefront integrations are announced and unshipped. Each one converts a waiting-list market into an addressable one.
  • A commercial vehicle in SaudiA registration and a bank account a Saudi gateway will settle into — the gate in front of the second market.
  • An operator, not an engineerSomeone to run merchant success while the platform keeps being built. The scarce resource here has never been code.
